name: Erik Mesic
headline: Student at NYU Stern — Accounting | CPA Track — Pre-Law
summary: I study accounting and the intersection of business, law, and governance. My work spans legislative advocacy, educational reform, debate, and quantitative research.

projects.name: RAISE Act Legislative Advocacy
projects.description: Policy design and fiscal modeling to improve education funding.
projects.overview: A policy-focused project examining the RAISE Act through the lenses of education funding, legislative advocacy, and fiscal modeling.
projects.role: Policy research, legislative analysis, and quantitative modeling.
details: Examined the policy design and funding implications of the proposal.
Translated policy questions into a quantitative modeling framework.
Developed advocacy-oriented materials to communicate the proposal clearly.

projects.name: LLM Stability Research
projects.description: Hierarchical models and variance analysis on LLM outputs.
projects.overview: An empirical research project investigating the stability and variance of large-language-model outputs using hierarchical statistical methods.
projects.role: Research design, statistical analysis, and interpretation.
details: Designed a framework for comparing variation across model outputs.
Applied hierarchical modeling to separate sources of variance.
Focused on reproducible quantitative analysis rather than anecdotal model behavior.

projects.name: Assessing Tucson Property
projects.description: Quantitative investment analysis and MCMC modeling.
projects.overview: A quantitative real-estate analysis using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods to evaluate property-level assumptions and investment risk.
projects.role: Investment analysis, modeling, and risk assessment.
details: Built a probabilistic framework for evaluating uncertain property outcomes.
Used MCMC simulation to explore distributions rather than relying on point estimates.
Connected quantitative results to practical investment and asset-management decisions.

experience.title: Strategic Real Estate and Investments Analyst
bullets: Executing Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations for portfolio risk assessment.
Planning and overseeing the divestment of over $500,000 from equity to diversified asset classes.
Assessing rental property management options following a distressed situation.
